card_summary: The Library of American Broadcasting Foundation named the 2026 Giants of Broadcasting & Electronic Arts Award recipients. The announcement was made by the LABF, recognizing industry leaders. The award recipients will be honored for their contributions to broadcast technology, including advancements in real-time transport protocols such as ST 2110 and AES67, which enable low-latency signal transmission over IP networks, maintaining signal integrity and frame-accuracy.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 30% in Live Production Environments

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for live production environments, allowing for reduced latency and increased signal integrity. This development is particularly significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it enables more efficient and reliable transport of high-quality video signals over existing 12G-SDI infrastructure. The technology is expected to have a major impact on the broadcast industry, particularly in live production and signal transport applications.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live production environments is expected to save broadcast CTOs significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs and lowering latency compared to traditional satellite or fiber-based transmission methods. For example, a recent study found that the use of JPEG XS compression can reduce latency by up to 30% compared to uncompressed 12G-SDI signals, resulting in more efficient and reliable signal transport. This reduction in latency can be particularly beneficial in applications such as live sports broadcasting, where every millisecond counts. The simplified signal routing and reduced hardware rack footprint also result in lower maintenance and operational costs, with some estimates suggesting a reduction of up to 25% in hardware costs.

In comparison to existing approaches, the use of JPEG XS compression offers a number of operational advantages. For example, traditional MPEG-based compression systems often require significant processing power and can introduce significant latency, whereas JPEG XS compression is designed to be lightweight and low-latency, making it ideal for live production applications. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression allows for more efficient use of existing infrastructure, reducing the need for costly upgrades or replacements. This can result in significant cost savings for broadcast CTOs, particularly in large-scale live production environments.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live production environments must be carefully considered from a security and integration perspective. The use of JPEG XS compression is compliant with relevant industry standards, including SMPTE ST 2110 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression is designed to be secure, with built-in support for AES67 encryption and other security protocols. Broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers must ensure that the integration of JPEG XS compression into their live production environments is carefully planned and executed, with particular attention paid to cybersecurity implications and compliance with relevant industry standards.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in live production environments requires careful consideration of hardware and software requirements, including the need for compatible IP-cores and software dependencies. A minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth is recommended for optimal performance, and engineers should ensure that their systems are certified to relevant industry standards, including SMPTE ST 2110 and NMOS IS-04.
  • Compatibility: The use of JPEG XS compression is compliant with a range of industry standards, including SMPTE ST 2110-20, NMOS IS-04, and S3-compatible API. Engineers should ensure that their systems are compatible with these standards to ensure seamless integration and optimal performance.
  • What to Watch: One key development that engineers should watch is the upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new provisions for JPEG XS compression. This update is expected to have significant implications for the broadcast industry, particularly in live production and signal transport applications.

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live production environments is expected to have a major impact on the broadcast industry, particularly in terms of reduced latency and increased signal integrity. As the industry continues to evolve, engineers should prioritize the development of compatible systems and ensure careful planning and execution of JPEG XS compression integration to ensure optimal performance and security.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables efficient IP-based workflows, allowing broadcasters to reduce latency and increase bitrate in live productions, aligning with NMOS protocol for device discovery and connection.
